correctness.rationale: Every geodesic has at most two edges and each edge extends to a two-edge geodesic because every part has at least two vertices. Count all labelled directed pair-center types by exact multinomial pairing, with no orientation duplicates. A packing is inclusion-maximal exactly when remaining part occupancies have no two-from-one/one-from-another pattern. For all-doubleton parts, maximal configurations have precisely two disjoint unused-vertex cases, both counted by explicit factorial terms; all support sizes form the stated interval, implying the pure-order list. Direct independent finite path enumeration checks 18 general profiles and six doubleton profiles; proof establishes full quantifiers.

value.rationale: This classification determines all feasible and facet cardinality counts of maximal-geodesic packing complexes on an infinite multipartite family, not merely packing numbers. On a natural symmetrical all-doubleton specialization it gives a complete factorial facet polynomial, a gap-free facet cardinality spectrum, and the structural reentrant purity pattern: r=6 nonpure, r=7 pure, r>=8 nonpure. The cases are motivated by maximal geodesic path packings and cannot be read from scalar biclique results.
